diseases.name: Fire Blight
diseases.description: A bacterial disease that blackens raspberry shoot tips and leaves, as if scorched by fire.
diseases.causes: Bacteria spread by rain, insects and pruning tools in warm, humid weather, entering through flowers and wounds.
symptoms: Shoot tips wilt, blacken and bend over like a shepherd's crook
Leaves turn brown-black but stay on the cane
Fruit stays small, dry and hard
diseases.effect: Blighted shoots and their fruit are lost.
diseases.untreated: Infection can move down the cane.

steps.title: Cut out blighted shoots
steps.instruction: Cut 15-20 cm below the damage in dry weather and remove the prunings.
steps.rationale: Removes the bacteria before they spread.

steps.title: Disinfect pruning tools
steps.instruction: Wipe tools with disinfectant between cuts.

prevention.title: Check shoot tips in warm, wet weather

lifecycle: Bacteria survive in cankers on host plants.
Rain and insects carry them to flowers and shoots.
Shoot tips blacken and bend over.
Ooze from the shoots spreads them further.
conditions: Apple or pear trees with fire blight nearby.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: raspberry fire blight
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Gray Mold
diseases.description: Grey mould of raspberry fruit, the main cause of rotting berries.
diseases.causes: The fungus lives on dead plant material; its spores infect flowers in wet weather and the berries rot as they ripen.
symptoms: Soft, light-brown rot on the berries
Grey, fuzzy mould covering the fruit
Rot spreads quickly between touching berries
diseases.effect: Fruit rots on the cane and soon after picking.
diseases.untreated: Most of a wet season's crop can be lost.

steps.title: Remove mouldy berries
steps.instruction: Pick off mouldy berries when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Pick often and cool the fruit
steps.instruction: Pick every day or two and chill the berries.
steps.rationale: Ripe fruit is most at risk.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide at flowering on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Thin canes and keep rows narrow

lifecycle: The fungus lives on dead plant material.
Spores infect the flowers in wet weather.
The berries rot as they ripen.
Grey spores spread to neighbouring fruit.
conditions: Wet weather at flowering and harvest.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: raspberry gray mold
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of raspberries and blackberries.
diseases.causes: Spores from infected leaves and canes spread by rain splash in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Heavily spotted leaves yellow and drop
diseases.effect: Leaf loss weakens the canes for next season.

steps.title: Remove spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Thin the canes
steps.instruction: Remove weak and old canes after harvest.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Remove old canes and fallen leaves

lifecycle: The fungus overwinters on leaves and canes.
Rain splashes spores onto new leaves.
Purple spots with pale centres form.
conditions: Old canes left in the row.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: raspberry leaf spot
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Yellow Rust
diseases.description: A rust fungus of raspberry leaves and canes.
diseases.causes: Spores overwinter on fallen leaves and canes and infect new leaves in spring; summer spores spread in humid weather.
symptoms: Small yellow spots on the upper leaf
Bright yellow-orange pustules on the underside
Pustules turn black late in the season; leaves drop
diseases.effect: Leaves fall early, weakening the canes.
diseases.untreated: Severe years reduce the next crop.

steps.title: Remove rusted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off rusted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Remove old fruited canes
steps.instruction: Cut out fruited canes after harvest.
steps.rationale: They carry the fungus over winter.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores overwinter on leaves and canes.
In spring they infect new leaves.
Black winter spores form in autumn.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: raspberry yellow rust
